text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Coles Myer Ltd has reported a 5.4 per cent increase in first-half sales to A$9.94 billion, defying one of Australia's toughest retail trading periods. The result was in line with market expectations and indicated the company would report slightly improved first-half earnings of around A$200 million; a result underpinned by the supermarket and liquor divisions. Page 19.

In the first step in a restructuring program, troubled dairy group National Foods Ltd has sold consumer products division NationalPak for A$206 million, with a view to refocussing National Foods on its core business. US-based First Brands Corporation hasbought NationalPak, and the profit generated from the sale will be reinvested in core business activities of food and beverages for National Foods. Page 19.

Cultus Petroleum has confirmed that a 20 metre oil column with a substantial gas cap has been discovered in the Cornea 2 oil area in Western Australia. An additional 10 metre hydrocarbon bearing sequence has also been discovered lower in the well. The dicovery has sparked interest among oil explorers bidding for offshore acreage adjacent to the WA 241P permit. Page 20.

Century Drilling Ltd predicts it will post revenues of A$99.34 million in the year to June. The specialist drilling contractor provides drilling services to major corporates working in the oil and gas, mineral and geothermal sectors in Australia, Indonesia and the Philippines and claims industry fundamentals will continue to increase its earnings. Page 20.

Queensland casino operator Jupiters Ltd has revealed a 148 per cent jump in December-half net profit to A$20.16 million. The figures are in stark contrast to the figures posted in the same period last year, where the company posted a profit of only A$8.12 million. The profit was aided by the halving of the high-roller gaming tax to 10 per cent from July 1 last year. Page 21.

Investment guru Kerr Neilson's listed investment Platinum Capital Ltd has suffered a slump in profit largely due to a failure to predict the extraordinary rise in the US share market. Profits fell to A$759,000 in the six months to December 1996 from A$5. million in the previous corresponding period. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer and one of its smallest competitors Harris Scarfe Holdings Ltd have both confirmed encouraging half-year sales results, indicating the retail sector is picking-up. Coles Myer sales grew 5.2 per cent to A$5.5 billion and discount department store Harris Scarfe reported sales up 15.6 per cent to A$123.6 million. Page 21.

Indonesia's love affair with the clove flavoured cigarette Kretek has meant the owners, the Wonowidjojo family, have moved into the number seven spot on The Australian's Asian Top 100 billionaires list. The company has more than doubled its estimated net orth to US$7.7 billion, after rating only 27th last year with US$3 billion. Page 21.

Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane has told the Australian Securities Commission's Electronic Commerce Conference that electronic commerce will never attract sufficient funds to become a force in the financial sector requiring central bank supervision. Macfarlane said he could see finance on the Internet developing but doubts the system will ever rival conventional cash or bank deposits. Page 21.

Shares in the Commonwealth Bank leapt to record levels yesterday as investors anxiously await the announcement of the Bank's interim profit next week. ABN Amro-Hoare Govett banking analyst Michael Pulman said it would not be a surprise for the Bank to shw a strong first-half profit. Page 22.

Despite Tony Richter's Formulab Neuronetics Corp Ltd delaying its $A20 million-plus listing on New York's Nasdaq index, directors are confident of signing off a prospectus later in the week. The share issue was due to be completed on Tueday, but the Perth-based technology group confirmed yesterday it had been granted approval by the Australian Stock Exchange to extend the deadline to complete its Nasdaq listing by two months. Page 22.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) forecasts that natural gas will increase from 18 per cent of the nation's energy consumption last year, to 28 per cent by 2010. Executive Director of ABARE, Brian Fischer, said yesterday at the groups' annual Outlook conference in Canberra, that the growth rate in consumption across all energy sources was expected due to a general economic decline and increased energy efficiencies. Page 23
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

St George Bank chairman Frank Conroy has expressed concerns over the return of loose commercial lending practices which plagued the banking sector in the 1980's and lead to banks sustaining large losses. Conroy made the comments at the conclusion of St George's annual meeting, when the bank indicated it may lose more than the estimated 1,000 staff in its merger with Advance Bank. Page 29.

While Australia follows the 'Mark Booth' court case involving Macquarie Bank executive director Simon Hannes, it is understood that the cases of two companies investigated by the Australian Securities Commission last year after they made big profits on TNT options trading - Cardy and Company Pty Ltd and Blaironia Pty Ltd - remain open. Page 29.

Industry cries for a change in administration of the superannuation surcharge have been ignored by the Federal Government, prompting warnings of higher fees for all superannuation members. The surcharge will force funds to collect tax file numbers from mebers and in some cases hold two accounts for members. Page 29.

BT Australia head Rohan Hedley has confirmed BT Australia will vote against a proposed acquisition by Brierley Investments Ltd of a further 4.99 per cent of John Fairfax Holdings from Canadian Press baron Conrad Black. BT claims they fail to see how the move will improve the position of its investors. Page 29.

One of the world's top management consultants KPMG Barents has been recruited by ANZ Ltd to orchestrate massive cost efficiencies at the bank to counteract possible takeover bids later this year. The Washington-based company will supply specialist consultants to provide strategic and logistic support to senior executives. Page 29.

The Australian Stock Exchange has made preliminary investigations into Shaw Stockbroking's capital adequacy following the loss of $A3 million through and exchange-traded option strategy that involved some of the firm's clients taking a position in anticiption of a sharemarket price correction. However, there is no concern the Sydney broker cannot cover any costs. Page 31.
THE AGE

Busy Christmas trading and steady January sales have contributed to Coles Myers' half-year sales revenue rising 5.4 per cent to $A9.945 billion in a slow retail market. New chief executive Dennis Eck said the results were satisfactory in the fae of the company's extensive restructuring and the group remained cautiously optimistic. Page B1

Washington-based KPMG Barents, one of the world's top management consultants, has been recruited by ANZ Bank to provide a team of consultants to orchestrate extensive cost efficiencies at the Bank in order to build a defence against possible takeover bidslater in the year. The group will provide strategic and logistical support to senior executives with ANZ chief executive Don Mercer overseeing what has been described as the 'global transformation program'. Page B1

There is industry speculation Telstra's 1996 projected A$30 billion float will be affected by a shortfall in 1996-7 earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) with long distance call problems, a slowing economy and bad debts named as threats to the telecommunications carrier's 1997 earnings. The company's earnings struggle may serve as a reminder of the potential of competition to hurt the company. Page B1

The All Ordinaries were lifted to a higher close yesterday of 2435.8, up 26.7 points with blue-chips leading the way, prompted by lingering optimism of a forthcoming interest rate cut and rebounding by major stocks. Meanwhile the March contract of the Share Price Index climbed 37 points to 2440 with 9690 lots traded - the first time in two weeks it has closed at a premium to the equities market. Page B2.

Stockholders of Platinum Capital, the investment company set up by former BT whiz-kid Kerr Neilson, have witnessed a steady erosion of the share price since late 1995. Floated three years ago at one dollar, the stock is now only fetching 85 cents compared with asset backing of $1.01. Page B2.

BT Australia, John Fairfax's 14 per cent shareholder, is to vote against Brierley Investments' acquisition of another 5 per cent of Fairfax from Canadian press baron Conrad Black. In December 1996, Brierley paid Black's telegraph group $A447 million for 9.9 per cent of Fairfax, a deal which took Brierley to the takeover threshold but left it short of the 25 per cent foreign investment guidelines allows it to own. Page B3.
